task3_cleansing_audit.classification_basis: AGENTS.md section 5: release and cleansing are separate; copies, partial state and failure paths count; salts/IVs/names/UKM are public unless they key secret state

gaps.statement: x942kdf_set_buffer replaces the previous buffer with a plain CRYPTO_free, and it is the helper that installs the X942 secret. Re-setting OSSL_KDF_PARAM_SECRET/KEY on an X942 context therefore frees the previous secret without cleansing it, while the final x942kdf_reset (:2356) does cleanse. The same file's SSKDF path (via src/params/mod.rs:2994) and HMACDRBG path (:9307-9345) do cleanse, so X942 is internally inconsistent. Authority-identical (OpenSSL x942kdf.c plain-frees the old secret); AGENTS section 5 forbids reproducing release-without-cleanse.

ossl_cms_EncryptedContent_init overwrites ec->key with a fresh OwnedBuf and never releases or cleanses the incumbent; the next line sets ec->keylen unconditionally. Reachable through CMS_EncryptedData_set1_key(cms, NULL, ...) / CMS_EncryptedData_decrypt called twice on the same CMS (src/cms/cms_smime.rs:576-620). The final free cleanses keylen bytes (src/cms/cms_asn1.rs:544), so a replaced key is freed or leaked without being zeroized, and a future key==NULL call on a keyed ec would desynchronise the cleanse extent. Authority-identical (cms_enc.c:203-230).
gaps.severity: secret-retention + latent extent desync (not UB today)

gaps.statement: CMS_RecipientInfo_set0_password assigns pwri->pass/passlen without releasing or cleansing the incumbent, and its documentation (unlike CMS_RecipientInfo_set0_key's, src/cms/cms_env.rs:2068-2110) does not state that replacement detaches rather than releases. A caller that transferred a passphrase and then re-associates or clears with NULL orphans an uncleansed passphrase copy. Authority-identical (cms_pwri.c:22-37).

KeySlot::install replaces the KEK slot without releasing the incumbent. This is documented and authority-identical, and is required to let CMS_decrypt_set1_key detach a borrowed buffer; recorded as a retained caller obligation, not a defect.

task3_cleansing_audit.outside_scope_residual: derived keys handed to EVP_CIPHER_CTX/EVP_MAC_CTX/EVP_PKEY are released by those subsystems' own free paths, which this audit did not open; they remain an unresolved dependency for any secret-memory claim about CMS/KDF.
task3_cleansing_audit.verdict: RAND_CMS_STORE_KEYFMT secret-memory residual moves from unaudited to AUDITED WITH GAPS: RAND (ctx, DRBG state, pool, seed, I/O buffers), STORE (passphrase data/cache, PKCS#12 temporary) and most of KDF cleanse on release and on failure. Three concrete release-without-cleanse paths remain (G1 KDF/X942, G2 CMS content key, G3 CMS password), all authority-identical and therefore compatibility-preserving but not safe. The mechanism cannot be SAFETY_DISCHARGED for secret memory.

mechanism_impact.new_defect: MIRI-UB-1 invalidates the call_item_exp contract for eight ADB accessors (CMS, EC, PKCS#7, PKCS#12, X.509 policy). Any mechanism whose closure includes src/asn1/utl.rs:89 (at minimum CMS, X.509 and the shared ASN.1 mechanism) cannot be SAFETY_DISCHARGED until the ABI is corrected: criterion 1 (an explicit validity contract per unsafe op) is not met when the contract states the wrong ABI.
mechanism_impact.rand_cms_store_keyfmt: no verdict flips to discharged; the secret-cleansing residual is now specific (G1-G3) instead of unexamined, and remains OPEN.
mechanism_impact.asan: no verdict change: 42/42 focused tests clean with a firing Rust canary supports 'no detected fault on these paths', which is not a safety certificate (AGENTS section 8).
mechanism_impact.stop_condition: AGENTS section 6 STOP applies to MIRI-UB-1: a confirmed memory-safety defect. The narrowest BOUNDARY check is a review of every Asn1Template.item writer for ABI-typed accessors plus a Miri rerun of the affected item families after repair. This receipt does not fix source.
